editions.label: 09 Sep
editions.title: Foreign trio bets €87M on 245 Portuguese homes — outside Lisbon prime
editions.summary: Foreign capital is moving past Lisbon prime — and into the mid-market. A new three-founder firm, Nova Atlantic, is committing €87 million to build 245 homes across Sintra, Gaia and Viana do Castelo, with units from €165,000. In Porto, a design-led Foz tower (Belfoz) hit 100% reservations in 45 days. And from 1 September, Portugal's new affordable-rent regime hands landlords a full income-tax exemption if rents sit at or below 80% of the municipal median. Commercial investment, meanwhile, is running at €1.4 billion for the half-year — hotels leading, offices sliding. Net: the money is broadening — down the value chain, out of the capital, and increasingly shaped by tax policy.

editions.label: 08 Sep
editions.title: Spain's Alfana buys Forum Algarve for €130M — its first deal abroad
editions.summary: Alfana Investment Management is buying Forum Algarve for about €130 million — the Spanish manager's first-ever deal outside Spain. The Faro centre is a trophy: 27,400 sqm, 115 shops, near-100% occupancy and 7.8 million visitors a year. Santander private-wealth clients funded it, with the signing set for Lisbon this week. Elsewhere, capital keeps chasing scarce prime stock — Lisbon prime rents rose 7.6% in H1, second only to Cape Town worldwide. And the rulebook is shifting: the Bank of Portugal's new 45% loan-to-income cap took effect on 1 August, while a fresh decree overhauls public-works procurement from 1 October. Net: retail and residential are where conviction sits; regulation is the variable to watch.

editions.label: 07 Sep
editions.title: Portugal tops the world on house prices: +15.2%, No.1 of 57 economies
editions.summary: Portugal posted the world's steepest real house-price growth in Q1 — up 15.2% year-on-year, first of 57 economies tracked by the Bank for International Settlements. Globally, real prices actually fell 1.2%; the eurozone managed just 2.6%. Capital is following the heat: commercial investment hit €1.41bn in H1, up 14%, led by hotels at €508M. Lisbon apartments now average €5,850/m² (+16%), Porto €4,180 (+13%). Retail dealmaking is back too — Spain's Alfana bought Faro's Forum Algarve for €130M, its first move abroad. Net: demand still vastly outruns supply, and foreign money is leaning in, not out.

editions.label: 6 Sep
editions.title: Alfana buys Forum Algarve for €130M — Spain's first bet outside home turf
editions.summary: Spain's Alfana bought Forum Algarve for around €130M — its first deal outside its home market, and Commerz Real's exit from the 27,400 sqm Faro centre. Retail keeps proving it can move at scale even as prime offices stay starved of stock. In Lisbon, BPI Gestão de Ativos sold a Saldanha office block for residential conversion, the latest in a wave that turned roughly a fifth of 2025 office deals into change-of-use plays. On the supply side, BPI now expects 2026 home completions to hit a 16-year high near 27,900 units. Porto and Matosinhos are both leaning in, funding more than 2,000 affordable rental homes between them. Net: capital is chasing retail and hospitality while the housing machine finally speeds up — but prime offices remain the market's tightest squeeze.

editions.label: 05 Sep
editions.title: Sines' €20bn industrial boom outruns its housing — government steps in
editions.summary: Sines is Portugal's boomtown — and its cautionary tale. More than €20bn of private industrial investment, led by Repsol's Alba petrochemical complex and the Start Campus data centres, has the town up 12% in population since 2021 — with no rentals below €2,000 and nothing to buy under €300,000. The government has now unveiled a special plan to fund housing, schools and health services alongside the private money. Elsewhere the squeeze is turning into pricing power: Lisbon prime office rents rose 10.3% — the fastest in Europe — as Grade A vacancy fell to a record 0.7%. And Porto gained a heavyweight, as ex-city housing chief Pedro Baganha joined Dils to lead Cities & Investment. Net: industrial and office demand is real, but Portugal's binding constraint everywhere is the same — not enough built space.

editions.label: 04 Sep
editions.title: Portugal's rent tax cut (25%→10%) costs €303M as August rents jump 4.9%
editions.summary: Capital keeps coming — but Portugal's market is splitting by asset and by price. Commercial investment hit €1.41bn in H1, up 14%, yet capital is turning selective — Lisbon office occupancy fell 20% even as prime apartments pushed to €5,850/m². Lisbon has now put a €303M price tag on its rental-tax package, cutting IRS on moderate rents from 25% to 10% and construction IVA from 23% to 6%. Rents answered by rising 4.9% in August — a second straight monthly gain that breaks the first-half slide. And Spain's Alfana bought Faro's Forum Algarve from Commerzbank for €130M, its first deal abroad. Net: money and demand are both firm, but the winners are narrowing to the right asset at the right price.

editions.label: 3 Sep
editions.title: Rental overhaul heads to Parliament: faster evictions, old rents thaw
editions.summary: Portugal is about to rewrite the rules of renting. The government's NRAU rental overhaul is now before Parliament. It lets landlords unfreeze pre-1990 rents when the original tenant dies, and fast-tracks evictions after two months of arrears. Ministers point to roughly 250,000 well-kept vacant homes they hope to coax back onto the market. Investors read it as a structural tilt toward landlords — and toward liquidity in a segment that has been frozen for decades. Meanwhile capital keeps arriving: hotel investment tripled to 519M euros in H1 and commercial volumes rose 14% to 1.41bn euros. Net: the rules are loosening just as money crowds into Portuguese bricks.

editions.label: 2 Sep
editions.title: Portugal draws €1.4bn in H1 as offices flip to flats; CBRE eyes €2.4bn year
editions.summary: Foreign capital is back in Portugal — and it's rebuilding the city it buys. Commercial real-estate investment hit €1.4 billion in the first half of 2026, and CBRE now expects the full year to reach €2.4 billion. The money isn't just buying — it's repositioning. Roughly a fifth of office deals now target a change of use, and BPI just sold a 4,500 sqm Saldanha block to be turned into premium flats. Municipalities are moving too: Vila Franca de Xira wants to triple its Lisboa-Norte logistics platform for data centres and 5,000 jobs. And distressed stock is surfacing, with Novo Banco putting Luís Filipe Vieira's portfolio on the block. Net: the capital is deep, but the return is increasingly in the conversion, not the trophy.
